item.title: No EC nod needed for voter to sue candidate over false information: Supreme Court
item.description: A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the Karnataka HC order which had held that “right given to the voter is only to file an election petition, and not to register a private complaint of crime which is the duty of the Election Commission, if it wants to do so”.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: Farooq Abdullah's comments on Pakistan and Kashmir draw flak
item.description: Farooq urged NC workers and legislators to remain loyal to the party, whether in power or not, as he touched on a range of issues in his speech. “Hold on to the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you remain truthful and stand up for what is right, your future will never be secure,” the veteran said.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: Princess’s gambit: At 11, Bodhana Sivanandan is an international master
item.description: Sivanandan, who lives in the London suburb of Harrow, broke the 38-year-old record held by Hungarian chess legend Judit Polgar, widely regarded as the greatest female player in chess history, after winning her final-round game at the European Women’s Club Cup in Budva, Montenegro on Friday. Polgar had qualified at the age of 12 in 1988.
item.dc:creator: NAOMI CANTON

item.title: Interview | ‘AAP had 4.5 years to end drug menace, gangsterism in Punjab’: Pilot
item.description: "BJP has no strong footing in Punjab and has survived on the back of SAD support. But SAD has also split and is facing internal issues. It is not the force like they were under Badal Senior. It will be a bipolar contest over who can lead Punjab better. There will be other players like Amritpal Singh’s party, but people of Punjab don’t give a fractured mandate," Sachin Pilot said.
item.dc:creator: SUBODH GHILDIYAL

item.title: Michael and Susan Dell’s foundation spotlights free skills training in Texas
item.description: The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation has reported remarkable achievements among graduates of its skilled-trades training initiatives. Over a dedicated five-week course crafted with input from employers, participants secure jobs almost immediately. Success stories like Mariah showcase a transition into well-paying, stable careers, while Skillpoint Alliance is enhancing training capacities to address Texas's rising need for skilled workers, ultimately promoting economic growth and assisting businesses in meeting workforce challenges.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Suspicious pigeon with coded ring, Pak currency causes a flutter in Jammu
item.description: An official pointed out that such episodes are not uncommon in border areas of J&K and Punjab, where pigeons have been used for smuggling or for sending messages across the frontier. On Saturday, the pigeon was found near a temple in Samba’s border area of Mawa around 6.40am and was immediately captured by locals after they spotted a ring tied to its leg.
item.dc:creator: SANJAY KHAJURIA

item.title: Dallas insurer paid $4,261 for floor damage; court rejects $58,150 claim
item.description: A federal appeals court has ruled against Dallas residents who sought over $58,000 from State Farm for water damage from a 2021 freeze, determining that their lawsuit was not filed within the required timeframe of their insurance policy. State Farm had already compensated for initial damages but denied further claims, especially since the homeowners declined additional living costs during property repairs.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Defer Nov 1 rally, will hit festive business, traders urge Rahul; BJP raps Congress
item.description: CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said Delhi records Rs 25,000 crore in business on Dhanteras across major sectors. CTI claimed that traders suffered losses of Rs 3,000 crore in Oct due to rallies and road closures in Connaught Place, India Gate and central Delhi. BJP claimed some Congress allies have disagreed with Rahul Gandhi’s decision to hold the rally on Nov 1.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Daughter’s inheritance rights can’t be defeated by limitation: J&K and Ladakh HC
item.description: The dispute dates back to Sept 14, 1982, when Themu, daughter of late Sonu, filed a civil suit claiming half share in land measuring 58 kanals and 11 marlas left behind by her father. She challenged mutation no. 43 dated Oct 15, 1966, which had been entered exclusively in favour of one Shib Devi and sought declaration of her inheritance rights along with consequential possession.
item.dc:creator: SANJAY KHAJURIA

item.title: CBI files FIR against IL&FS Energy, top execs in Rs 212cr Canara Bank loan fraud case
item.description: CBI has named M/s IL&FS Energy Development Company Ltd, its MD and directors — Sunil Wadhwa, Anoop Seth, Hari Sankaran, Ramesh Chandra Bawa and Arun Kumar Saha — and unknown public servants and private individuals as accused. The case was registered on Oct 21 following a complaint by Canara Bank’s circle office in Bandra.
item.dc:creator: RAJ SHEKHAR JHA

item.title: Scientists correct 155-year-old solar storm mix-up: Train delay was in 184
item.description: A fascinating correction has emerged from the archives concerning a train delay in Exeter. Initially reported incorrectly, researchers have clarified that the incident actually transpired on October 18, 1848. This revelation was achieved through the analysis of railway records and contemporary newspapers, alongside geomagnetic data, which pointed to a significant solar storm influencing the delay during that time.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Mississippi sinks 31-ton propane tank and steel tower to build fish reef
item.description: A 31-ton propane tank and steel tower once used for firefighter training in Mississippi have been sunk about 13 miles offshore to create an artificial reef for marine life. Supported by Chevron and local organisations, the project aims to provide shelter for fish and improve fishing opportunities. A similar reef created in 2023 now supports more than 530 red snapper, according to official estimates.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Bezos’s parents invested $245,573 in Amazon when it was an uncertain online bookstore
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Baltimore house sold for $310,000, later listed for $35,000 after foreclosure
item.description: In 2022, a property in Baltimore purchased for $43,000 astonishingly changed hands for $310,000 just a year later. This sharp spike in valuation has led to accusations of inflated property prices by investors, resulting in numerous foreclosures. Federal lawsuits allege a scheme involving over 150 properties generating millions in loans, prompting lender scrutiny and investigations into the housing market, revealing Baltimore's deep-seated issues with housing insecurity.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Govt to explore ways to draw desi researchers back to India: Piyush Goyal
item.description: After meeting a group of Indian researchers in Berlin Friday, Goyal said the challenge goes beyond financial incentives to creating a supportive ecosystem for research and innovation. He intended to discuss the issue with govt, educational institutions, academia, research institutions and industry in order to forge stronger partnerships, he said.
item.dc:creator: ATUL MATHUR

item.title: Congress alleges attack on Christian families in Bengal, writes to Amit Shah
item.description: Congress general secretary K C Venugopal has written to Union Home Minister Amit Shah and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, on Saturday, seeking urgent action over the alleged assault, humiliation and coercion of three Christian families in Patlapur village of Paschim Medinipur district during Durga Puja celebrations.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Natalia Granada reveals how her family inspired her F1 Academy journey
item.description: Natalia Granada takes her first plunge into the F1 Academy, marking a pivotal chapter in her racing narrative. With her family's enthusiasm for Formula 1 as her driving force, she transitioned from go-karting into the fast lane. Juggling education with rigorous training, she receives backing from the Iron Dames organization.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: How Ons Jabeur went from hotel tennis courts to Grand Slam finals
item.description: Ons Jabeur’s journey from makeshift courts in hotels in Tunisia to three Grand Slam singles finals is a tale of years of determination, family sacrifice and belief in her distinctive playing style. Jabeur, the first Arab woman to play in a Grand Slam singles final, has broken with tennis tradition and set the stage for young players from Tunisia, North Africa and the wider Arab world.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: ED moves Supreme Court against HC order to quash case against portal, founder
item.description: The directorate, which filed an appeal almost five months after the HC pronounced the order on May 29, also took the ground that the HC passed the order five months and 26 days after the judgement was reserved and it was in violation of SC’s guidelines that the verdict should be delivered within three months.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: Rs 10 lakh cover for 45 paise: Counter rail ticket buyers get insurance option
item.description: The scheme has provision for payment of Rs 7.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and up to Rs 2 lakh for hospitalisation expenses arising from injuries, as well as Rs 10,000 towards transportation of mortal remains of deceased passengers. The Railway Board has directed all its zones to implement the facility.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Set to expand cabinet, J&K CM Omar asks hopefuls not to ‘mob or spam’ him
item.description: J&K CM Omar Abdullah advised them against knocking on his doors or that of his father and National Conference president, Dr Farooq Abdullah, to lobby for ministerial positions. After meeting Sinha, Omar told reporters he sought an appointment with him for next week so that he can make changes and expand his council of ministers.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: Over 4 lakh march across country, nearly 1,000 arrested - France protests in videos
item.description: In France, protesters took to the streets, decrying the plight of underfunded schools and spiraling living expenses. This unrest sparked violent confrontations with the police in major cities like Paris and Lyon, where authorities resorted to tear gas and water cannons. As arrests mounted, President Macron's administration faces an escalating challenge, with students and teachers uniting to demand improvements in education and address deep-seated economic disparities affecting their communities.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah flights hit: Air India, IndiGo extend suspensions
item.dc:creator: VIVEK DUBEY

item.title: 'Act of treason': BJP guns for Farooq Abdullah over 'Pak protecting Kashmiris' remark
item.description: In recent developments, BJP leaders have taken strong issue with Farooq Abdullah's comments regarding Pakistan's alleged support for Kashmiris. Abdullah, speaking at a workers' gathering, cast doubt on the central government's approach to Jammu and Kashmir, raising questions about India's commitment to justice. In response, BJP representatives charged him with treason, claiming his remarks weaken India's stance on the issue.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: 'Can no longer breathe': Thousands protest in Turkey over media crackdown
item.description: Thousands demonstrated in Istanbul and Ankara to oppose the government's increasing restrictions on independent media and journalists. Protesters called for press freedom, chanting slogans that emphasized their demand for basic rights. Various media professionals have been arrested recently, raising concerns about freedom of speech in Turkey. Journalists and activists participated in these rallies to highlight the public's right to information.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Fake faces, stolen voices, false stories: Can we still trust what we see online?
item.description: Recent incidents highlight how Artificial Intelligence can create deceptive videos and audio that mislead individuals. Eye-witness accounts and authentic recordings can no longer be trusted without verification. High-profile figures have been especially targeted in various scams that exploit technology. It is essential for individuals to adopt cautious practices to combat misinformation effectively. Building digital awareness will help in preserving trust and accountability in online interactions.
item.dc:creator: YASHIKA BAJAJ

item.title: Delhi school death: Police recover 3-page suicide note, breakup angle under probe
item.description: An 18-year-old Class 12 student was found burnt on her school premises in Krishna Nagar, Delhi. Police recovered a three-page suicide note, which mentioned family and a friend. Investigators are examining potential motives, including a possible breakup or conspiracy. Family members express disbelief at the possibility of suicide and suspect foul play. The police are pursuing leads and reviewing CCTV footage to understand the circumstances surrounding her death.
item.dc:creator: VRITI JAIN

item.title: 'We are fed up, Macron must give in': Protests erupt across France; cops use tear gas
item.description: France is taking significant measures to manage mounting tensions, deploying around 70,000 police officers to supervise protests over education funding and escalating living costs. In response to previous violent outbreaks, authorities have restricted protest routes. Major Parisian museums and shops have temporarily closed to prevent potential chaos as demands for enhanced educational opportunities, better salaries, and improved public services grow.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: 'Boys becoming men': Gambhir's message after Tilak-Nitish pull off thrilling chase
item.description: In an impressive display, India clinched a stunning four-wicket victory over New Zealand in the second T20I at Christchurch, taking a pivotal 2-0 lead in the series. After a wobbly middle order, Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy stepped up in the chase, while Naman Dhir's quick 31 runs helped stabilize the innings.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.dc:creator: VIVEK DUBEY

item.title: BFI power struggle deepens ahead of October 28 meeting; Boxing fraternity calls for unity
item.description: Indian boxing is currently undergoing administrative disputes amid a potential no-confidence motion against president Ajay Singh. Key figures in boxing are urging for stability and accountability to protect the sport's growth. An ad-hoc committee has been formed in Jharkhand to address the local association's election issues. BFI secretary general Pramod Kumar has proposed the no-confidence motion to be considered soon.
item.dc:creator: SABI HUSSAIN

item.title: Haryana student beaten with iron rods; CCTV captures 50 blows in a minute
item.description: Rudra, a BBA student, suffered severe injuries after being attacked by three men following a motorcycle collision. The incident occurred around 7 pm near Hudda Park in Bhiwani district, causing multiple fractures and serious injuries. CCTV footage reportedly shows the assailants attacking Rudra with sticks and an iron rod while he attempted to escape. His family believes the assault was linked to a previous altercation involving his elder brother Dhruv.
item.dc:creator: MANOJ DHAKA

item.title: ‘What’s with the hate?’: Kriti Sanon reacts to backlash over her Raksha Bandhan ad outfit
item.description: Kriti Sanon, trolled in August over her “revealing” outfit in a GIVA Raksha Bandhan ad, says her choli became a “national debate.” Speaking to Kareena Kapoor Khan, she said women are scrutinised for everything, criticised those preaching culture while abusing her family online, and added women simply want to not be judged.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Pollard doesn't want to see 'yellows and reds', urges MI to put 'team above self'
item.description: Pollard, who was Mumbai Indians' batting coach for the last four IPL seasons, takes over from Mahela Jayawardene, who parted ways with the franchise last week. The former West Indies all-rounder has been associated with MI since IPL 2010, when he was signed as a player.
item.dc:creator: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI

item.title: 45 paise for Rs 10L cover: Rlys extends insurance to counter tickets from Oct 27
item.description: Starting October 27, Indian Railways will provide travelers the option to include an Optional Travel Insurance Scheme with their reservation ticket purchases. For a nominal fee of just 45 paise, passengers gain crucial coverage for accident-related incidents. The insurance offers various payout options tailored to medical and logistical emergencies. Reservation staff will be responsible for informing ticket buyers about this crucial add-on before finalizing bookings.
item.dc:creator: ARVIND CHAUHAN

item.title: Tensions mount at Jamia: Classes shift online; AISA alleges assault on students
item.description: "All Deans/Heads/Directors and faculty members as well as all bonafide students are hereby directed to adhere to the online class schedule and ensure regular participation in academic activities. All faculty members are requested to make the necessary arrangements for conducting classes through online platforms and to provide students with the required academic support and learning materials," the notice read.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: US midterms: At Florida rally, Trump vows action against Cuba after Iran war
item.dc:creator: AASHISH VASHISTHA

item.title: Cong to launch door-to-door campaign, hold marches over voter list 'discrepancies'
item.description: Congress aims to register all eligible citizens by the end of December through an extensive campaign. The campaign will include marches, pamphlet distribution, and awareness meetings in both urban and rural areas. Booth-level agents will be appointed to help verify the accuracy of voter lists and report discrepancies. Allegations have arisen regarding significant irregularities affecting millions of voters across the country.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Tilak Varma reveals Gambhir's message that inspired him during thrilling chase
item.description: Tilak Varma shone brightly with an unbeaten 51 runs, leading India to a thrilling victory over New Zealand. Inspired by encouraging words from coaches Gautam Gambhir and Sitanshu Kotak, he anchored the innings in a tense chase, with Nitish Kumar Reddy supporting him with a vital 26 runs. India's last-ball triumph secured a 2-0 lead in the five-match T20I series, highlighting their impressive form.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY
